Population.evidence_source: The objective of the interviewer was "to get to know the elderly person" from the informants' narratives, as far as this was possible. The first question was worded as follows: "Can you tell me how you experienced him/her?" The interviewer structured the conversations to cover the topics of major lifetime events, health, aging, personality traits and the social context, including relationships. The open structure of the interviews also encouraged the informants to take up topics they viewed as important in their account of the deceased. The interviews usually lasted approximately two hours and were tape-recorded in their entirety. They took place two to six months after the suicide, as recommended by Beskow et al. (1990).

Type.evidence_source: Most of the interviews with relatives were held in their homes. Doctors and healthcare staff were interviewed at their workplaces. All the interviews were conducted by the first author, who is a specialist in internal medicine/geriatrics and has long clinical experience.
